how NCERT reaches this answer: states answer

new NCERT · BIO12L ch4 · printed page 022

BIO12L-CH04-P88 · 4.8.2 Mendelian Disorders
Haemophilia : This sex linked recessive disease, which shows its transmission from unaffected carrier female to some of the male progeny has been widely studied. In this disease, a single protein that is a part of the cascade of proteins involved in the clotting of blood is affected. Due to this, in an affected individual a simple cut will result in non-stop bleeding. The heterozygous female (carrier) for haemophilia may transmit the disease to sons. The possibility of a female becoming a haemophilic is extremely rare because mother of such a female has to be at least carrier and the father should be haemophilic (unviable in the later stage of life). The family pedigree of Queen Victoria shows a number of haemophilic descendents as she was a carrier of the disease.

new NCERT · BIO12L ch4 · printed page 023

BIO12L-CH04-P94 · 4.8.3 Chromosomal Disorders
Failure of segregation of chromatids during cell division cycle results in the gain or loss of a chromosome(s), called aneuploidy. For example, Down’s syndrome results in the gain of extra copy of chromosome 21. Similarly, Turner’s syndrome results due to loss of an X chromosome in human females. Failure of cytokinesis after telophase stage of cell division results in an increase in a whole set of chromosomes in an organism and, this phenomenon is known as polyploidy. This condition is often seen in plants.

new NCERT · BIO12L ch4 · printed page 023

BIO12L-CH04-P91 · 4.8.2 Mendelian Disorders
Phenylketonuria : This inborn error of metabolism is also inherited as the autosomal recessive trait. The affected individual lacks an enzyme that converts the amino acid phenylalanine into tyrosine. As a result of this phenylalanine is accumulated and converted into phenylpyruvic acid and other derivatives. Accumulation of these in brain results in mental retardation. These are also excreted through urine because of its poor absorption by kidney.

new NCERT · BIO12L ch4 · printed page 022

BIO12L-CH04-P89 · 4.8.2 Mendelian Disorders
Sickle-cell anaemia : This is an autosome linked recessive trait that can be transmitted from parents to the offspring when both the partners are carrier for the gene (or heterozygous). The disease is controlled by a single pair of allele, HbA and HbS. Out of the three possible genotypes only homozygous individuals for HbS (HbSHbS) show the diseased phenotype. Heterozygous (HbAHbS) individuals appear apparently unaffected but they are carrier of the disease as there is 50 per cent probability of transmission of the mutant gene to the progeny, thus exhibiting sickle-cell trait (Figure 4.15). The defect is caused by the substitution of Glutamic acid (Glu) by Valine (Val) at the sixth position of the beta globin chain of the haemoglobin molecule. The substitution of amino acid in the globin protein results due to the single base substitution at the sixth codon of the beta globin gene from GAG to GUG. The mutant haemoglobin molecule undergoes polymerisation under low oxygen tension causing the change in the shape of the RBC from biconcave disc to elongated sickle like structure (Figure 4.15).

why this chapterThe answer depends on integrating Joule heating, H = integral of i^2 R dt with i = dQ/dt, over the time until the current falls to zero.
subtopic 1Electrical Energy and Power
why this subtopicThe answer depends on Joule heating for a time-varying current, H = integral of i^2*R dt with i = dQ/dt = a - 2bt, and on stopping the integration at t = a/2b where the current falls to zero, which gives H = a^3*R/(6b).
difficultyhard · 4 steps
stepsdifferentiate the given charge to get the current, I = dQ/dt = a - 2bt → recognise that the current falls to zero at t = a/(2b) and that this, not infinity, is the upper limit over which 'total heat' is to be accumulated → set up the heat integral H = integral of I^2 R dt from 0 to a/(2b) → expand (a - 2bt)^2 and evaluate the integral to get a^3 R / (6b)
whyThe work is a differentiation, a decision about the limit of integration, and then a polynomial integral that has to be expanded and evaluated term by term.
the catchThe upper limit has to be found rather than read off the stem - the question never says when the process stops - and the three wrong options (a^3R/3b, a^3R/2b, a^3R/b) are exactly the values produced by the usual slips in choosing that limit or in expanding the square.

A body of mass 1 kg begins to move under the action of a time dependent force F⃗ = (2t î + 3t2 ĵ) N, where î and ĵ are unit vectors along x and y axis. What power will be developed by the force at the time t?
  1. (2t2 + 4t4) W
  2. (2t3 + 3t4) W
  3. (2t3 + 3t5) W
  4. (2t2 + 3t3) W
2What the answer rests onthe NCERT page as printed, beside that page's extracted text with the quoted line marked. For Physics and Physical Chemistry, the concept and the approach instead — a numerical's answer is a value NCERT never prints.
conceptP = F · v
approachDivide the given force by the 1 kg mass to get a(t), integrate from rest to get v(t), then dot F with v to get the power developed at time t.
also usesa = F/m  ·  v = ∫ a dt

subjectPhysics
chapterWork, Energy and Power high confidence
why this chapterThe answer depends on instantaneous power P = F.v, with v obtained by integrating the time-dependent force over mass.
subtopic 1Power
why this subtopicThe answer depends on instantaneous power being the dot product P = F . v, with v obtained by integrating the time-dependent force (v = t^2 i + t^3 j for a 1 kg body starting from rest), which gives P = 2t(t^2) + 3t^2(t^3) = 2t^3 + 3t^5 W.
difficultyhard · 4 steps
stepsget the acceleration from the force, a = F/m, with m = 1 kg so the components are 2t and 3t^2 → integrate each component with respect to time from rest, using 'begins to move' as the zero initial velocity, to get v = (t^2)i + (t^3)j → form the power as the dot product P = F . v, component by component → multiply out and collect: 2t(t^2) + 3t^2(t^3)
whyThe work is a calculus chain - divide by the mass, integrate a time-dependent force to velocity, then take a vector dot product and simplify - none of which can be short-cut by a stated formula.
the catchEach option is a plausible pair of powers, so the exponents do the discriminating and a single slip in the integration of the 3t^2 component lands on a printed option rather than on nothing.
